channel.title: Block Club Chicago - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Block Club Chicago (blockclubchicago.org)

item.title: How You Can Help Morgan Park High School's Band Following Missed Trips Due To Costs
item.description: The parent-led nonprofit set a $50,000 goal to cover expenses for the Morgan Park High School band, which canceled an Atlanta trip and a performance in the South Side Irish Parade due to a lack of funding.

item.title: Rat Birth Control Is Working In Wicker Park, Early Results Show
item.description: With early data pointing to a reduction of rat activity in the area, organizers said they will continue the program and even expand it to other parts of Wicker Park and Bucktown. A similar effort is underway in Lincoln Park.

item.title: Uncommon Ground Owners Retiring After 35 Years In Lakeview
item.description: Mike and Helen Cameron hope to find a new operator to carry on the cafe's legacy of farm-to-table food, intimate musical performances and community.

item.title: GoFundMe Launched For Mother Killed In Garfield Park Shooting: 'Everybody Loved Brandy'
item.description: Brandy Fleming, 29, was found unresponsive near the alley by her home, police and her family said. Her family is raising money for her funeral and to care for her 5-year-old son.

item.title: Definition Theatre Won’t Let Racist Vandalism Stop Them From Amplifying Black Voices
item.description: The incident is being investigated as a hate crime. But the Black woman-led theater is continuing its work — and just wrapped one of its most successful shows in years.

item.title: Ann Sather Closing On Belmont Avenue After 81 Years, But Aims To Remain In Neighborhood
item.description: A proposal for a new apartment building on the block initially spared the restaurant from having to move. But now construction will cause the Belmont Avenue building to be demolished.

item.title: State's Attorney Calls Petition For Special Prosecutor To Investigate ICE Abuses 'Illogical'
item.description: In a court filing, Cook County State's Attorney Eileen O’Neill Burke said the petition backed by a coalition of elected officials and community groups is a "heavy-handed attempt" to "usurp" her authority.

item.title: Judge Orders Feds To Release $3 Billion For CTA Projects: Reports
item.description: The CTA filed a lawsuit last week against the federal transit agencies over their decision to freeze over $3 billion in funding for two major Red Line projects over concerns about “race-based contracting.”

item.title: $10,000 Reward For Info Offered After UPS Driver, Dad Of 3 Killed in Auburn Gresham
item.description: Michael Hunter was looking for the person who stole his truck when he was shot and killed Sunday near 80th and Hermitage, police and family members said. “Someone knows something.”

item.title: City Moves To Landmark Edgewater's Bryn Mawr Historic District
item.description: The district includes Bryn Mawr Avenue from Broadway to Sheridan Road and famed residences like the Edgewater Beach Apartments. An initial hearing is April 2 with the city's landmarks commission.

item.title: Robots Gone Wild: Food Delivery Robots Smash 2 Bus Shelters In Chicago
item.description: A Coco delivery robot collided with an Old Town bus shelter on Tuesday afternoon, just days after a Serve Robotics robot did the same thing in West Town.

item.title: An AI School, With No Teachers, To Open in Chicago This Fall
item.description: Alpha School, a pricey private school with campuses nationwide, uses artificial intelligence to instruct students. AI schools have been praised by the Trump administration, but researchers say there's limited evidence the model works.

item.title: Winnemac Park Debuts Artificial Turf Fields, Ready For Spring Sports
item.description: Improved drainage and other upgrades to the park’s baseball and soccer fields will prevent them from becoming muddy swamps after rain. A ribbon cutting is April 10.

item.title: 24 Easter Egg Hunts, Bunny Photos And Brunches Across Chicago
item.description: Chicago is celebrating Easter with egg hunts, art classes, a matcha tasting and more.

item.title: Luna Y Cielo, Logan Square’s Bilingual Play Cafe, Closing This Weekend After 3 Rocky Years
item.description: The playroom almost closed twice in 2024 due to lack of business. Owner Vanessa Ávalos said health issues are behind her decision to close now.
